intent: Transition from an upright standing idle with lowered arms into a lower fight idle: both hands rise into guard, the stance opens and bends more, and the center of mass lowers. This is a stance transition, not an attack or a locomotion cycle.

phases.description: Leave standing idle and prepare the stance; the pelvis shifts slightly and the arms begin to leave their lowered position.
Both arms accelerate upward and inward in front of the torso to form the guard, while torso rotation becomes more pronounced.
Lower the center of mass and complete the fight stance; the strongest right-leg adjustment occurs around f15, and the guard continues locking in through f23.
Settle into the lower fight idle; the pelvis reaches its lowest region around f25 and movement then decreases.

keyPoses.role: Standing idle: upright torso with lowered arms.
Fastest upper-body transition: torso and both arms reach peak angular activity for the frame.
Hips reach their maximum +X position; the strongest right-leg adjustment occurs as the fight stance locks in.
Guard is nearly complete; the pelvis is already deeply lowered and the left arm reaches its largest pose-departure region.
Fight idle at the end of the transition: lower stance with movement settled.

weightTransfer: The pelvis makes a small preparatory shift toward -X through f4, moves toward +X and reaches its maximum at f15, then recenters while lowering strongly. Hips Z reaches its lowest point at f25 and stays near that low level through f30. The evidence is not sufficient to assign a definite support or weight-bearing foot.
bodyMechanics: Overlapping coordination sequence: stance/pelvis preparation -> torso and both arms accelerate into guard, peaking at f10 -> the right leg makes its strongest adjustment to lock the stance, peaking at f15 -> the guard continues to complete while the pelvis lowers and recenters through f23-f25 -> settle through f30. This describes observed timing and coordination, not a causal power chain.

recommended: Transition from standing idle to fight/combat idle.
Timing for raising both hands into guard while lowering the center of mass and opening the stance.
Pelvis weight-shift behavior when entering a combat stance.
